summary: This program asks whether you want to enter the temperature in Celsius, converts from Fahrenheit when you say no, and then advises what to wear based on the result.

lines.text: The answer is cleaned up with .strip() to drop stray spaces and .lower() to ignore capitalisation, then compared to "yes"; the comparison produces True or False, so use_celsius holds a boolean rather than text.
A boolean variable can be tested directly, with no comparison needed — this reads almost like an English sentence.
input always hands back text, so float converts it into a number that can be compared and used in arithmetic.
The Fahrenheit reading is stored under its own name to keep it distinct from the Celsius value used later.
This is the standard Fahrenheit-to-Celsius formula, so that both branches leave temp in the same units.
Only after the two branches have agreed on a Celsius value does the advice logic begin.
elif is only reached when the first test failed, so this check quietly means "between 10 and 30 was ruled out".
The else branch catches every temperature that neither earlier test claimed, guaranteeing exactly one message is printed.
